subject: Customer report: reserved throughput mismatch and GPU pool saturation
messages:
From: Ethan Wallace <ewallace@bluelayer.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@bluelayer.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 03:12:00 +0000
Subject: High error rate and slowdowns on reserved pool — urgent

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing a sudden spike in 5xx errors and p95 latency on our production routes served from our reserved capacity (reservation id: RB-8342). The first alert fired at ~02:58 UTC and it's been sustained for ~40 minutes. Key observations: 
- P95 latency jumped from ~180ms to ~950ms for text-gen calls.
- 5xx rate for the last 15m is ~7.2% (normal <0.3%).
- The customer dashboard shows reserved throughput consumed, but the effective throughput (responses/sec) is much lower than expected.

We've attached a small error sample and a short trace (bluelayer_error_snip.log) — you'll see repeated timeouts and some KV-cache stalls. This is impacting our main workflow; customers are failing requests across multiple regions but primarily us-east-1.

Can your team confirm whether this is a dedicated pool saturation issue or something in the reserved routing layer? We need a quick mitigation (fallback or burst) and an ETA for full recovery. We're also tracking this on our side and can share additional logs.

Thanks,
Ethan
Head of Platform Engineering
BlueLayer AI

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Wallace <ewallace@bluelayer.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 03:21:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High error rate and slowdowns on reserved pool — urgent

Ethan — thanks for the heads up and the log sample. I'm escalating immediately and we will open a joint bridge.

Immediate plan:
- Stand up an urgent ops call in 10 minutes (03:30 UTC) — internal + BlueLayer.
- Priyom / David please surface pool metrics (GPU util, queue depth, KV cache backlog) and any recent config changes.
- Marissa / Vivek — procurement/ops: please confirm burst authorization path for BlueLayer (DL-8342) and whether we can enable a temporary +25% burst on their reservation.
- I'll keep Ethan/Sasha updated and share an initial impact summary after first triage.

Ethan — as an immediate mitigation, can you confirm whether switching to the smaller text-compact-v2 variant for low-priority requests is acceptable for 30–60 minutes while we triage? If yes, we'll prepare a routing rule and a rate-limited fallback.

I've attached a one-page initial-impact-summary for your ops team.

Rachel
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ethan Wallace <ewallace@bluelayer.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 03:38:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High error rate and slowdowns on reserved pool — urgent

Quick findings from the bridge and early metric pulls: 
- GPU farm: nodes assigned to RB-8342 show sustained 99% SM utilization on the hot POD set; queue depth spiked from ~12 -> ~220.
- KV cache evictions increased 8x; tail latencies on cache lookups correlate with the 5xxs.
- Autoscaler did not trigger additional pods because the reservation cap was enforced at the service layer (we have a hard cap).
- I see a batch job (internal batch-id: batch-ingest-7791) that started at 02:45 UTC generating large multi-turn requests; it consumed very large batch sizes and pinned many KV shards. That job appears to be the primary driver.

Immediate mitigations we can execute now (5–15m):
1) Throttle or kill batch-ingest-7791 jobs (ops can reduce max_batch_size to 4) — reduces KV pressure.
2) Lift reservation cap temporarily with emergency burst (+25% compute) for RB-8342 and route priority traffic to the burst pool. We need Marissa/Vivek approval for burst cost.
3) Enable model-variant fallback rule: route non-critical requests to text-compact-v2 (estimated ~40% lower token cost and ~30% lower GPU utilization).
4) Clear a subset of KV cache shards to reduce evictions (will cause a short warmup but reduce tail).

I've uploaded a CSV with the pulled metrics: pool_metrics_2027-05-07.csv. Next steps: I'll implement (1) and (3) immediately if we have ops signoff. I'll coordinate on (2) once procurement confirms.

- Priyom
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Ethan Wallace <ewallace@bluelayer.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 08:27:00 +0000
Subject: Executive brief: BlueLayer reserved throughput mismatch and remediation plan

Marissa / Vivek — quick executive summary and ask. Looping Ethan for visibility.

What happened: an internal batch job at BlueLayer (multi-turn ingestion) started producing very large batches at ~02:45 UTC which pinned KV shards and saturated the reserved GPU PODs for reservation RB-8342. Autoscaling did not expand capacity because the reservation was capped at the service level; result was queueing, KV-cache thrashing and elevated 5xxs and p95s.

Impact: production traffic for BlueLayer degraded ~03:00–03:45 UTC, customer-visible errors peaked at 7.2% and p95 latency approached 1s. Mission-critical flows were affected for ~25 minutes.

Actions taken (complete/in-progress):
- Priyom throttled the batch job and reduced max_batch_size (complete).
- We applied the model-variant fallback routing for non-critical requests to text-compact-v2 (in-progress).
- Cleared a subset of KV cache shards to relieve lookups (in-progress).
- BlueLayer agreed to pause high-batch jobs for the next 2 hours.

Ask / decision point:
1) Approve emergency burst for RB-8342: temporary +25% reserved compute for up to 3 hours (cost approx. $9.5k). This buys breathing room and avoids further customer errors while ingestion patterns normalize.
2) Approve a short-term credit of one week's overage for BlueLayer while we run a post-incident runbook and remediation plan. This is primarily a customer retention ask.

If approved I'll: (a) trigger the burst immediately and (b) draft the customer-facing post-incident note with root cause and follow-up commitments.

Thanks — Rachel
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
